uses.use: to draft tokens for a larger Carbon model that checks them, so the pair generates DNA faster with the larger model's output unchanged
uses.source: its model card: "intended primarily as a draft model for speculative decoding", paired with Carbon-3B or Carbon-8B, and "not designed to be competitive with the 3B/8B Carbon models on downstream benchmarks"
uses.measured: how well it predicts DNA text read alone, a perplexity; a drafter is judged by how many of its tokens the larger model accepts and the time that saves
uses.needs: a larger Carbon model for it to draft for. None is on this machine; Carbon-3B is a download of roughly 6 GB, an estimate from its size at bfloat16, and is the owner's to approve. The drafting itself is built, and internal/inference TestCarbonSpeculativeChain holds the draft side alone until then

uses.use: to read a picture of a document, one page or many, and write out its text and layout
uses.source: its model card: an image-text-to-text model for "one-shot long-horizon parsing", whose every example hands it a picture with the prompt "document parsing."
uses.measured: general-knowledge multiple choice asked of its text decoder alone, with no picture; the reading stands beside what a constant answer scores, and says whether the decoder is a general assistant and nothing about how it reads a page
uses.needs: pictures of documents with the text they hold, scored by the share of characters read wrongly, and the picture path served and scored, where today the record is of the text decoder alone. No such set is on this machine; a public one is the owner's to approve as a download

uses.use: to draw and edit infographics: large pictures dense with small text, laid out as a page
uses.source: its model card: "designed for integrated infographic generation and editing", recommended at 50 steps with a guidance scale of 4, at 2048 by 2048 by default and 2720 by 1536 in its example
uses.measured: whether a judge finds in the picture what the caption of a photograph named, with each picture drawn as its maker recommends, at 2048 by 2048 in 50 steps with a guidance scale of 4 and a timestep shift of 3; no question asks whether text in the picture can be read. A picture at those settings takes about two minutes to draw, and the row's first-output time is of a smaller and faster request than the reading's pictures
uses.needs: nothing more to exist: the drawn-text measure asks for stated text, draws it at the model's own size and steps, and has a model that reads text say whether the text asked for is the text drawn; this model is read on it, and that reading heads its row in place of this one. Its twenty briefs of five short texts are easier than the pages the model's card shows, so a set with more and smaller text is what a harder reading of its use needs

uses.use: to carry what it read across separate passes in eight notes it writes to itself, its only memory of anything before the 512 tokens in front of it; a research model built to test that, and by its card "not an assistant"
uses.source: its model card, whose headline measure is how much the carried notes help it predict the opening of a chunk it has not seen, against the same model with the notes reset: 9.42 nats on code and 7.27 on web text
uses.measured: the perplexity of encyclopedia passages read 512 tokens at a time, each window from empty notes, so the memory the model exists for is never written or read. The card gives one figure of this kind, a perplexity of 94 on web text, which is the nearest thing the reading can be set beside, on another corpus
uses.needs: nothing that is not on this machine: the card's own measure, the loss on a held-out document's next chunk with the notes carried and with them reset, over the passages already scored. It needs the deferred-continuation turn served, which the scoring path does not do today

uses.use: to reason about a physical scene for a robot: answer questions over pictures and video, predict the frames an action leads to, and plan a task as steps with a picture of each goal
uses.source: its model card: "a unified multimodal foundation model for embodied cognition"; its own benchmark, RxBrain-Bench, is listed there as not yet released
uses.measured: whether its description of a video frame shares more words with the frame's own caption than with three others; it answers no lettered question, so nothing is asked of its reasoning, and neither its predicted frames nor its plans are looked at
uses.needs: its maker's benchmark, which is not released, or a set of questions about scenes and actions with known answers; neither is on this machine, and the first cannot be downloaded yet

uses.use: to change what an instruction names in a video and leave the rest of it as it was
uses.source: its model card: it edits "while preserving backgrounds and non-edited regions", and its own test case changes one fruit in a bowl into another
uses.measured: changes to the whole clip, a pencil sketch, a cartoon, night, rain, snow, fog, which leave no region unedited to preserve; the judge is asked one question of each clip, whether it shows what it showed with the change made
uses.needs: nothing that is not on this machine: instructions that change one thing in a clip, with the thing and the rest of the clip checked apart, built from the clips on disk with the installed judge. It is the plan's next step for this model if a clip costs minutes

uses.use: not stated anywhere on this machine
uses.source: no documentation ships with it: a weights file of 120 kB, a configuration for a picture of 2 by 2 pixels and three classes, and a provenance file that names only its family, un0
uses.measured: nothing; it takes a class and no words, so the generators' held-out evaluation cannot be asked of it
uses.needs: the owner to say what Un-0 is for, so a measure of that can be named, or that it is a fixture and leaves the scorecard
